history.historicalImportance: Gaya is one of the most ancient and sacred cities of India, revered in both Hinduism and Buddhism. It is internationally known for Bodh Gaya, where Lord Buddha attained enlightenment.
history.formationHistory: Gaya district was established on 3 October 1865 during British rule. The region has been an important centre since the Magadha Empire and later became a major religious, cultural and administrative hub of Bihar.
history.freedomMovement: The district actively participated in India's freedom movement through the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement and Quit India Movement. Many local freedom fighters contributed to the struggle against British rule.
history.archaeologicalImportance: The district contains numerous ancient temples, Buddhist monasteries, archaeological remains and heritage sites associated with the Maurya and Gupta periods.

geography.location: Gaya district is located in the southern part of Bihar in the Magadh region and is bordered by Jharkhand to the south.
geography.climate: Tropical climate with hot summers, monsoon rains and cool winters
geography.forests: Moderate forest cover, mainly in the southern and south-western parts of the district

specialEconomicFeatures: International tourism centred around Bodh Gaya
Religious tourism contributes significantly to the local economy

agriculture.dairyDevelopment: Dairy farming is an important supplementary source of income for rural households.
agriculture.fisheries: Fish farming is practiced in ponds, reservoirs and river-based water bodies across the district.

infrastructure.roadNetwork: Gaya has a well-developed road network connecting all major towns, blocks and neighboring districts.
infrastructure.airConnectivity: Gaya International Airport provides domestic and international flight connectivity, especially to Buddhist pilgrimage destinations.
infrastructure.publicTransport: Bihar State Road Transport Corporation (BSRTC), private buses, taxis, auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws operate across the district.
infrastructure.electricity: Most urban and rural areas have access to electricity under the Bihar power distribution network.
infrastructure.waterSupply: Urban areas receive piped water supply, while rural areas depend on hand pumps, tube wells and government water supply schemes.
infrastructure.internetConnectivity: 4G and 5G mobile services are available in most parts of the district, along with broadband connectivity in urban areas.

education.governmentSchools: More than 3,000 government primary, middle and secondary schools operate across the district.
education.privateSchools: Several CBSE, ICSE and Bihar Board affiliated private schools are located in Gaya district.

bankingAndFinance.digitalBanking: UPI, Internet Banking, Mobile Banking and AEPS services are widely available.

governanceAndPublicServices.districtAdministration: Gaya district is administered by the District Magistrate (DM) and supported by various district-level departments.
governanceAndPublicServices.policeAdministration: Law and order is maintained by Gaya Police under the Bihar Police Department.
governanceAndPublicServices.fireServices: Fire stations operate in Gaya, Bodh Gaya, Sherghati and other major towns of the district.
governanceAndPublicServices.publicDistributionSystem: Essential commodities are distributed through Fair Price Shops (FPS) under the Public Distribution System (PDS).
eGovernanceServices: Bihar Right to Public Services Portal

lawAndOrder.trafficPolice: Traffic Police regulate traffic and road safety across Gaya district.
lawAndOrder.disasterManagement: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), Gaya coordinates disaster preparedness, emergency response and relief operations.

environment.forestCover: Forest cover is limited, mainly in the southern hilly areas of Gaya district.

mediaAndCommunication.postalServices: India Post provides postal, Speed Post, parcel and financial services across Gaya district.
mediaAndCommunication.telecommunication: 4G and 5G mobile connectivity is available in most urban areas, while rural coverage is continuously expanding.
